[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/27 (Sat) 10:17  
[FACT] User is looking to learn more about the different languages spoken in India.  
[RELATIONSHIP] User recently met a guy from India named Rohan who speaks Hindi, Marathi, and English fluently.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] India has over 22 officially recognized languages and numerous dialects.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Hindi is the official language of India, along with English, and is the most widely spoken language in the country, with over 500 million speakers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Hindi is the lingua franca of India, used for communication across different regions and languages.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Hindi has its roots in Sanskrit and evolved from various dialects of the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-European language family.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Hindi was influenced by Persian, Arabic, and Turkish during the Mughal Empire (1526-1756).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The modern Hindi language emerged in the 19th century, with the Indian independence movement playing a significant role in its development and promotion.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Hindi is considered the language of national identity in India.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Hindi is used in Bollywood, literature, music, and is seen as a symbol of Indian national identity and unity.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Hindi is widely used for communication, education, and media in India.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Rohan's proficiency in Hindi and English reflects the importance of these languages in Indian society.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Marathi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in the state of Maharashtra, with around 83 million speakers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Marathi has its roots in the ancient language of Maharashtri and was influenced by Sanskrit, Prakrit, and Persian.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The modern Marathi language emerged in the 13th century, with the Bhakti movement playing a significant role in its development.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Marathi is an essential part of Maharashtrian culture and identity, used in literature, music, drama, and cuisine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Marathi is the primary language of communication in Maharashtra and is taught in schools and universities across the state.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Rohan's fluency in Marathi reflects his cultural roots and heritage.
